exchanges.question: What do the management changes (Doug and Troy elevated to co-presidents, Marianne's departure) mean for leadership development and Dimon's CEO tenure? Second: how sustainable are IB and markets strength, and how risk-on is the firm?
exchanges.answer: Dimon: board made two co-presidents to prepare them to do more; timetable unchanged; Marianne chose to retire rather than stay once she knew the plans; 'No mystery.' Barnum: IB fees were fine but not super peak by historical standards; there was some pull forward and large deals contributed meaningfully, but the pipeline is quite robust and activity seems to beget activity; declined to guide. Equities' particular events this quarter hard to imagine repeating; markets revenues elevated with more financial resource deployment. The market is extremely risk on and JPM is a taker of that, balancing client support with caution.

exchanges.question: Progress toward the 15% retail deposit market share goal and how higher-for-longer rates affect the pace of share gains. Follow-up: where is JPM in the investment cycle (branches, AI, bankers) and what does it mean for medium-term operating leverage?
exchanges.answer: Wholesale deposit growth strong in first half, outperforming expectations, helped by lending (BFI, data centers) creating deposits. Consumer deposit growth expectation of low single digits this year unchanged; strong net new checking offset by yield-seeking flows, which remain a risk given a more hawkish rate environment. No change to the 15% aspiration, seen as a long-term outcome of strategy. On expenses, Dimon said it is a complete continuation with no change expected; Barnum said JPM will always invest while delivering exceptional current returns; no operating leverage outlook given.

exchanges.question: Drivers and 3Q/4Q cadence of the upward NII ex-Markets revision and exit rate into next year. Follow-up: why is markets NII guided higher despite higher rates?
exchanges.answer: NII ex-Markets raised from $95 billion to $96.5 billion; implied second half suggests a higher exit run rate assuming forwards and current deposit expectations. Biggest driver is deposit balances across wholesale and consumer plus favorable mix; rates slightly higher at both ends; actual rate sensitivity likely above reported EAR due to consumer beta outperformance, mostly front end. Markets NII is liability sensitive but forecast up due to expected lower non-interest-bearing financed assets in the second half; also higher equity allocation to CIB moves roughly $150 million of NII from NII ex-Markets to markets NII, which would not be offset in NIR.

exchanges.question: What characteristics are Dimon and the board seeking in the next CEO? Is Dimon's remaining tenure fixed or rolling, with a longer stay as executive chair, given Marianne's departure read as an extension? Follow-up: what does 'no change in timing' mean?
exchanges.answer: Timing essentially the same and up to the board. Listed traits: management, people, analytical, detail, culture carrier, curiosity, heart, grit, soul, work ethic, ability to work with CEOs and prime ministers; 300,000 employees, 50,000 in branches, 150,000 in operating and call centers. Named two co-presidents, Jen Piepszak as COO and Mary Erdoes continuing to run AWM. Timetable is 'several years', 'a few years', plus or minus, totally up to the board.

exchanges.question: With negative adjusted operating leverage year to date, could expense growth slow and operating leverage emerge over the next few years given AI? Second: any update on regulatory proposals (G-SIB surcharge, Basel III)?
exchanges.answer: Dimon: margins went up this quarter; perpetual operating leverage is a 'crazy notion' and part of why banks failed 20 years ago; might see a slowdown in expense growth in 2027 or 2028; will spend where ROI is good; AI benefits ultimately accrue to customers. Regulation: four changes needed—remove double count in operational risk capital, remove double count in market risk capital ($80 billion+ of market risk capital vs biggest quarterly loss of $1.4 billion; CCAR market loss ~$14-15 billion), adjust G-SIB as intended since 2015, fix short-term wholesale funding; would hold 10% more if asked but not with falsely done numbers. Barnum: removing RWA from the STWF denominator disproportionately burdens banks with both markets and consumer businesses (JPM, Bank of America) versus former investment bank competitors.

exchanges.question: Is this as good as it gets, or is it earlier cycle given AI, defense spending and supply chains? Second: is there a rate tipping point where deposit volumes and betas change meaningfully?
exchanges.answer: Dimon: getting close to as good as it gets; don't know how long it lasts. Barnum: short answer is they don't really know; expected negative convexity in consumer rate paid by now but not experiencing it; at some point it kicks in. Stress tests model accelerating rate paid in a regime change; current EAR ignoring convexity could wrongly suggest a 7% rate environment is great, which would not hold if they had to reprice the deposit franchise. Dimon: they assume some of that in models.

exchanges.question: Isn't operating leverage positive in dollars with 15% revenue growth, and why is this 'as good as it gets'? Second: what gives confidence Troy, without consumer experience, is right to run the consumer bank?
exchanges.answer: Dimon agreed operating leverage was positive. Barnum: expense guidance revised up $2.5 billion; first-half capital markets complex outperformed expectations by $6.5 billion with $1.5 billion of associated additional expense already booked; implicitly added $1 billion for the second half, not to be read as a revenue view. Dimon: very healthy, exuberant market with high prices and volumes, unknown duration. On Troy: strong analytics, EQ, culture carrier, operations/technology expertise from the IB; cross-company experience important. Barnum corrected that Troy was an options trader, not an FX trader.

exchanges.question: Are AI efficiency benefits underestimated, and could banks restructure much leaner (as Block did cutting 40% of staff)? Follow-up: what was most exceptional in equities this quarter that may be hard to sustain?
exchanges.answer: Dimon: not a sensitive topic; expects huge efficiency in certain parts; almost 1,000 use cases, about 50 really important (risk, fraud, marketing, hedging, prospecting, note-taking, idea generation, document reading); discrete areas reduced jobs 30% or 40% with most offered jobs elsewhere; retraining; AI will be faster and dramatic but benefits accrue to customers, not a sustained 50% ROE; big topic at July offsite. Barnum: equities drivers were major IPOs, major index rebalancing, complicated Korean equity market dynamics, Asia activity and very active clients; statistically improbable to repeat that combination.

exchanges.question: What is the health of the Main Street consumer amid housing/rate fragility, and is CapEx broadening beyond AI? Follow-up: why buy back stock at three times tangible book rather than hold more excess capital, and what about M&A?
exchanges.answer: Some CapEx and loan growth appears non-AI but AI proliferates widely. Dimon: CapEx ~$4 trillion a year; AI CapEx went from $400 billion last year to $700 billion this year, projected a little over $1 trillion next year. Consumer: spend robust across income segments, tax refund tailwind, delinquencies a little lower than expected, little support for K-shape; negative real wage cohort a watch area; credit depends on labor market, surprisingly resilient. Capital: buy less as price rises; excess capital approximately $40 billion expected to deploy over time; won't tell the market what they'll do. Dimon: 'made a mistake' mentioning $20 billion, could do far more or nothing; goal is deploying capital at a 17% return; open to inorganic (adjacencies, data) but organic first; building Chase UK toward a European digital bank.

exchanges.question: Status, timing and target audience of the smart cash tool, and comments on paying more for money over time? Second: what are JPM's European consumer banking aspirations in aggregate?
exchanges.answer: Smart cash is still a test case relating to a narrow segment of accounts competing for investment and deposit business; tests coming out; 'You'll see something this year.' Europe: digital changed the calculus; Chase UK started 4 or 5 years ago with almost 3 million or 2.5 million UK customers; opened in Berlin, doing better in Germany than expected but not yet profitable; added investment products in the UK, likely to add elsewhere and probably credit card. Dream is a pan-European successful digital bank; patient.

exchanges.question: Are competitors' credit underwriting standards getting looser? Second: could regulatory stability arrive and enhance bank valuations?
exchanges.answer: Barnum: 'crazy' is a strong word; data center underwriting is a bellwether; JPM passed on some deals (power supply, tenant risk) under a precise framework; competitive but normal pressures; flexes for important clients but tries to hold the line. Dimon: described a very mild deterioration—revenue growth assumptions, expense add-backs, more PIK, weaker covenants, rollover risk—in some players; expects outliers in the next credit cycle. Barnum: regulatory stability desirable and getting closer; not convinced regulation is a major valuation drag for JPM. Dimon: Supreme Court decision on presidential removal power reduces flip-flopping; praised Bowman and Warsh reviewing rules; resolution and recovery does not work; discount window should be viewed differently.

exchanges.question: Beyond volume/revenue-related expense, is JPM raising other expense categories or pulling forward tech/marketing? Second: how nimble is CIB capital allocation, is it at peak, and are internal limits binding?
exchanges.answer: Some ups and downs including marketing strategy he would not disclose; main driver is volume and revenue-related expense. Token (AI model) expense trivial in the first half, forecast meaningful acceleration in the second half but full-year still trivial and partly budgeted; important for next year; use the right model for the right purpose including open source. Declined to discuss internal limits; capital allocation responds to client demand plus passive effects (volatility raising market risk capital, equity appreciation raising prime RWA); ample excess capital; system flush with capital but less with liquidity, liquidity regulation next on the agenda. Dimon: risk standards unchanged.
